records.full_text:
Cambodia
Prakas No. 346 providing for the procedures for Plant Quarantine Inspection.
This Regulation, consisting of 9 articles and 1 Annex, provides for the Procedures for Plant Quarantine Inspection. Articles 1-3 establishes the following matters: procedures for plant quarantine inspection of import, export and transit, in the Kingdom of Cambodia, of all kinds of plant quarantine materials for the purpose of preventing endemic quarantine pest as to protect agricultural production and biodiversity and facilitate international trading activities. Physical persons or legal persons who import, export and transit, in the Kingdom of Cambodia, any kinds of plant quarantine materials shall apply for inspection in accordance with the procedures of plant quarantine inspection and in compliance with all plant quarantine rules. Physical persons or legal persons who import any kinds of plant quarantine materials or intend to import any kinds of plant quarantine high risk goods (as determined in the Annex) shall fill in the application for plant quarantine inspection of import consignment at Plant Quarantine Inspection Office and attach with specific documents.

Pakistan (Khyber Pakhtunkhwa)
The Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Fisheries and Aquaculture Act, 2022 (Act No. XL of 2022).
An act to provide for the protection, preservation, conservation, regulation and management of fisheries biodiversity and aquaculture in the Province of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.
This Act provides for regulation and management of fisheries and aquaculture in the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province of Pakistan. The Act contains eight chapters: I. Preliminary; II. Directorate General of Fisheries; III. Fisheries Park, Sanctuaries and Power to Lease; IV. License, Permit and Special Permit; V. Offences, Arrest and Seizure; VI. Penalties and Punishments; VII. Trial of Fisheries Offences; and VIII. Miscellaneous.
Chapter I consists of short title, extent, commencement and definitions. Chapter II establishes the Directorate General of Fisheries to deal with all matters provided in this Act. It provides for the appointment of Inspectors of Fisheries. Chapter III provides for establishment of Fisheries Parks for recreation, education and research activities, and eco-tourism. It also empowers the government to declare any public water to be a sanctuary, in respect of such species of fish as mentioned in the First Schedule. The Director general may lease out the fishing right in public water and allow to install fish cages or other aquaculture related technologies.
Chapter IV contains provisions relating to licenses and permits in respect of activities in Chapter III. Chapter V provides for offences, arrest and seizure of persons and their catch, fishing gear etc. Chapter VI contains penalties and punishment for offences committed under the Act. Chapter VII provides for trial of fisheries related offences. Chapter VIII prohibits interference in duty by officers under the Act and allows the Director General to amend the First Schedule as required.
Entry into force notes
It shall come into force at once.

Australia
Great Barrier Reef Marine Park Regulations 2019.
These Regulations, consisting of 275 sections divided into 18 Parts and completed by six Schedules, prescribe all matters required or permitted by the Act to be prescribed or necessary or convenient to be prescribed for carrying out or giving effect to the Act. The Regulations regulate use of the Great Barrier Reef Marine Park (Marine Park) providing for the following: give effect to, and enforcing the observance of, the Great Barrier Reef Marine Park Zoning Plan 2003 (the Zoning Plan) and Plans of Management, which are made pursuant to the Act; grant permissions in the Marine Park, imposing conditions which permissions may be subject to, charging fees by the Authority in respect of permissions, keeping records relating to permissions and a regime for modification, revocation and suspension of permissions; accreditation of Traditional use of Marine Resources Agreements (TUMRAs) entered into between Traditional Owners in respect of the Marine Park; regulate discharge of sewage in the Marine Park; regulate property and things in the Marine Park; report by the Authority on the condition of the Region through the Outlook Report; regulate interactions with cetaceans in the Marine Park; regulate vessel activity in the Marine Park; and collect Environmental Management Charge (EMC) by commercial operators in the Marine Park.
Entry into force notes
These Regulations enter into force on 1 April 2019.

records.full_text:
Australia
Great Barrier Reef Marine Park Regulations 1983.- Repealed
These Regulations implement provisions of the Great Barrier Reef Marine Park Act. They consist of a comprehensive text of 293 regulations, divided into 19 Parts. Part 1 contains an interpretation section in which various zones and terms "prescribed activity", "zone" and "zoning plan" are defined. Part 2 regulates the conduct engaged in by persons under permit in or entry into zoned areas. Part 3 provides for zoning plans in respect of fishing and restricted use of a particular area called the Far Northern Section, whereas. The remaining Parts provide for discharge of sewage in, or into, the Marine Park, in particular from vessels (3A), activities in marine park in general (4), compulsory pilotage (5), bareboat operations (6), fees for permissions (7), environmental management charges (8), plans for specific areas (9-12), notification and review of decisions (13), infringement notices (14), and miscellaneous matters (15).
Entry into force notes
These Regulations enter into force on 7 November 1983.

records.full_text:
New Zealand
Hauraki Gulf Marine Park Act 2000 (Act No. 1 of 2000).
The purpose of this Act is to: (a) integrate the management of the natural, historic, and physical resources of the Hauraki Gulf, its islands, and catchments: (b) establish the Hauraki Gulf Marine Park: (c) establish objectives for the management of the Hauraki Gulf, its islands, and catchments: (d) recognise the historic, traditional, cultural, and spiritual relationship of the Tangata Whenua with the Hauraki Gulf and its islands: (e) establish the Hauraki Gulf Forum.
The Forum shall integrate the management and, where appropriate, to promote the conservation and management in a sustainable manner, of the natural, historic, and physical resources of the Hauraki Gulf, its islands, and catchments. Functions of the Forum are set out in section 17.

Zambia
International Game Park and Wildlife Act.- Repealed
An Act to provide for the establishment of the International Game Park; save where it is expressly provided to the contrary in this Act, to apply the provisions of the National Parks and Wildlife Act thereto; to provide for transfer or assignment of all or any of the powers, duties or functions conferred or imposed upon the Minister and the Director under the said Act; to provide for the appointment of wildlife officers and wildlife rangers; to provide for the establishment, composition, functions and duties of an Advisory Committee in place of the National Parks Board; and to provide for matters connected with or incidental to the foregoing.
The President may, by Statutory Order, declare any one or more of the areas of land within the Republic and mentioned in the Schedule to be a National Park, thereafter to be known as the International Game Park The provisions of this Act, the provisions of the National Parks and Wildlife Act and the Rules, Regulations and Orders made thereunder shall apply to the International Game Park. the Minister may, by statutory instrument, for the specified period transfer or assign to the person to whom the International Game Park is let on a lease (“lessee”) all or any of the powers, duties or functions conferred or imposed upon the Minister and the Directors of Wildlife, Fisheries and National Parks by the National Parks and Wildlife Act. For the purposes of this Act, the lessee shall have the power to engage during the specified period wildlife officers and wildlife rangers and there shall be established during the specified period an Advisory Committee in place of the National Parks Board mentioned in section eleven of the National Parks and Wildlife Act. records.full_text:
Democratic People's Republic of Korea
Act of the Democratic People’s Republic of Korea on Fisheries.
This Act provides for rules and regulations for the conservation and management of fisheries resources, and for the production and processing of fish products.
The State shall develop marine aquaculture and exert a lot of efforts to aquaculture in rivers, lakes and reservoirs in order to increase fisheries resources stocks.
The Act defines responsibilities of different relevant organs for the following: production and processing of fish products; making up of production and export plans of fishery products; allocation of fishing grounds; carrying out of scientific research on fisheries resources and investigation of fish stocks; distribution of the fry of marine animals and seedlings of seaweeds to aquaculture grounds; collection of data of marine production volume; preparation of plans for building fishing vessels; improvement of processing lines; monitoring and control on fisheries resources conservation; etc.
The Act further sets every April and July as months for the conservation of fisheries resources in order to conserve marine resources. In relation to fisheries resources conservation the central territorial environmental guidance organ shall arrange the following: fishery resources conservation areas; species of fishery resources to be conserved; conservation seasons of fishery resources by species; size of fishery resources to be caught or collected; prohibited fishing gear or methods.
The Act also specifies the relevant organs, enterprises and institutions responsible for the guidance and control over the management of fisheries.

Guam (USA)
Territorial Park System Regulations - Chapter 3 of Title 23 of the Guam Administrative Rules and Regulations.
These Regulations define parks and provide for the control and management of public parks and monuments.
The Regulations provide rules aiming at the protection of natural features of parks and prohibit certain activities in parks. Among other things, no person shall harm plant or animal life except with the permission of the Chief of Parks and Recreation and no person shall remove or destroy any form of marine life, living or dead, except fish according to Guam fishing legislation and allowed by these Regulations, within the boundaries of any park. Hunting and fishing may be permitted exceptionally the Chief.

records.full_text:
Australia
Great Barrier Reef Marine Park Act 1975.
An Act to establish a Great Barrier Reef Marine Park and for related purposes.
The Act establishes the Great Barrier Reef Marine Park and the Great Barrier Reef Marine Park Authority. The Act is divided into 10 Parts, i.e.: Preliminary (I); Establishment, functions and powers of the Great Barrier Reef Marine Park Authority (II); Constitution and Meetings of the Authority (III); The Great Barrier Reef Marine Park (V); Offences and penalties in relation to Great Barrier Reef Marine Park and Region (VAA); Collection of environmental management charge (VA); Plans of Management (VB); Administration (VI); Finance and reporting requirements (VII); Compulsory pilotage (VIIA); Enforcement (VIII); Miscellaneous (IX).
An Authority by the name of the Great Barrier Reef Marine Park Authority is established under section 6. The Authority shall prepare zoning plans for areas forming part of the Park declared under section 30, pursuant to section 31. Such plans shall be laid before Parliament. Zones shall be used only for permitted purposes. The Authority may also prepare plans of management for one or more areas, species or ecological communities in the Park (sect. 39X). The Governor-General must not make a Proclamation under section 344 of the Environment Protection and Biodiversity Conservation Act 1999 declaring an area in the Great Barrier Reef Region to be a Commonwealth reserve under that Act.
Entry into force notes
This Act enters into force on 20 June 1975.

records.full_text:
American Samoa (USA)
Establishment of Ofu-Vaoto marine park (Chapter 03 of Title 18).
This Act creates the Ofu Vaoto marine Park on the island of Ofu, American Samoa. The boundaries of the park are described. The purpose of the marine park is to protect its unique coral reef wildlife habitat. It is classified as a territorial natural preserve which shall remain unimproved and shall be within the American Samoa parks system, except that it may not be removed from the system or reclassified by the Governor or director of the Department of Parks and Recreation. No fishing or shellfish harvesting shall be permitted in the park except that residents of Ofu Island shall be permitted to fish and harvest shellfish as permitted by fisheries Laws and Regulations.
